P08-002.boundary_rationale: Onset: the sub-onset 'son of man' at Ezek.33.10 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם אֱמֹר֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֵּ֤ן אֲמַרְתֶּם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי פְשָׁעֵ֥ינוּ וְחַטֹּאתֵ֖ינוּ עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּבָ֛ם אֲנַ֥חְנוּ נְמַקִּ֖ים וְאֵ֥יךְ נִֽחְיֶֽה (oshb:Ezek.33.10) opens with the quoted popular saying it will refute, immediately following the samekh-marked close at oshb:Ezek.33.9; that far face carries the mark and no formula, while the near face is this re-address to the people, after the watchman charge given to the prophet. An oath-plus-utterance combination follows at Ezek.33.11 אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם חַי אָ֣נִי נְאֻ֣ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִם אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הָרָשָׁ֔ע כִּ֣י אִם בְּשׁ֥וּב רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ וְחָיָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ שׁ֜וּבוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֧ם הָרָעִ֛ים וְלָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּתוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.33.11), carrying its own pe mark; this is disclosed as close-grade material that is NOT final here, because the same disputation continues through a second 'son of man' sub-onset at Ezek.33.12 restating the principle for “the children of your people” (web:Ezek.33.12) and on through the righteous/wicked case-pairs of 33.14-19. Close: a second pe mark follows Ezek.33.20 וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י אִ֧ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֛יו אֶשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶתְכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.33.20), which restates the people's complaint verbatim against 33.17 -- the four pointed words לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י stand byte-identical in both verses (oshb:Ezek.33.17, oshb:Ezek.33.20; WLC/OSHB, single witness) -- and then adds YHWH's verdict (“I will judge every one of you after his ways” (web:Ezek.33.20)), which stands at 33.20 only and has no counterpart anywhere in 33.17, marking the disputation's true end. The section-mark witness records that this verse carries no sof pasuq; the editors' note stands in its place, 'We read punctuation in L differently from BHS,' immediately before the pe (single-witness). No boundary is argued from the absent mark, only from the pe that follows and the topical restatement it closes. The near face of that close is a verdict clause with no formula — the discourse close of the disputation — and a dateline opens the material past it; a close seam of that shape is what this row's medium_low records, whatever stands on its far face.
P08-002.strongest_rejected_alternative: The rival onset is the 'and you, son of man' (ve'attah) at Ezek.33.12, which re-addresses the hearers as בְּנֵֽי עַמְּךָ֙ where 33.10 has בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.33.10, oshb:Ezek.33.12; WLC/OSHB, single witness). That shift does not license a cut: the two titles name one audience inside one speech — the first stands at 33.10, 33.11 and 33.20, the second at 33.2, 33.12 and 33.17 — and it is the second that opens the chapter's whole address. The rival's own close-shaped cluster cannot supply the missing onset either: 33:11's utterance formula stands mid-verse, at word 5 of that verse's 25 counted from one, with independent imperatives running on after it. The pe recorded on 33:11 is disclosed for the rival as a paragraph mark, not as an onset. Independently, a cut there would leave 33:10-11, two verses that are not a complete word-event unit, and that bar holds the span whatever shape the rival has. The disputation therefore runs on as one 'you say ... but I say' unit across 33:10-20, which is the near face on both of this row's seams.
P08-002.device_notes: unit_type disputation_oracle fits 33.10-20 as one unit; no category deviation. Row runs 11 verses, above the 7-10 typical band, held at medium_low rather than split: the rival onset at 33.12 re-addresses the same audience under a second title and is not licensed, and a cut there would leave 33:10-11, under three verses and not a complete word-event unit. K/Q disclosure (single-witness): oshb:Ezek.33.13 carries one note, ketiv צדקתו / qere צִדְקֹתָיו֙, and oshb:Ezek.33.16 carries one note, ketiv חטאתו / qere חַטֹּאתָיו֙; each ketiv stands unpointed in the running text of this witness, each of the two notes carries two morpheme separators in the apparatus which are dropped from the forms as given here, and no boundary is argued from either Qere. Paseq (count-only, single-witness): Ezek.33.11 carries 2 occurrences; intra-verse position is unsourceable from the extract.

P08-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: MT 33:20 is followed by a pe (single-witness), corroborating the onset at 33:21, and that pe stands where the verse itself carries no sof pasuq. The onset's near face is the dateline, a licensed onset of its own; its far face carries that mark and no formula. The dateline at Ezek.33.21 וַיְהִ֞י בִּשְׁתֵּ֧י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֗ה בָּעֲשִׂרִ֛י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לְגָלוּתֵ֑נוּ בָּא אֵלַ֨י הַפָּלִ֧יט מִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר הֻכְּתָ֥ה הָעִֽיר (oshb:Ezek.33.21) — one of the book's 14 year-bearing oracle datelines and a hard seam — reports the fugitive's arrival with news the city has fallen. Ezek.33.22 וְיַד יְהוָה֩ הָיְתָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י בָּעֶ֗רֶב לִפְנֵי֙ בּ֣וֹא הַפָּלִ֔יט וַיִּפְתַּ֣ח אֶת פִּ֔י עַד בּ֥וֹא אֵלַ֖י בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיִּפָּ֣תַח פִּ֔י וְלֹ֥א נֶאֱלַ֖מְתִּי עֽוֹד (oshb:Ezek.33.22) follows with the hand-of-YHWH idiom (matched on the construct alone, one of 7 verses carrying the construct) and the mouth-opening event that fulfils the muteness first commissioned in ch. 3 and anticipated as a coming sign earlier in the book. This hand-of-YHWH occurrence opens no vision here — it is narrative notice, not a scene-transport marker. Close: a pe mark follows Ezek.33.22 (single-witness), and the verse completes the narrative beat before Ezek.33.23 opens a fresh, formally distinct word-event oracle; that close is two-faced, the hand-and-mouth-opening notice on its near face against the fresh word-event on its far face. A licensed near face at the onset with a mark-only far face behind it is the shape this row's medium records.
P08-003.device_notes: unit_type is a disclosed per-bytes deviation: classified commission_narrative (the muteness/mouth-opening device) rather than vision_report, because the hand-of-YHWH here is followed by narrative notice (the mouth-opening at Ezek.33.22) rather than any scene-transport or vision-inaugurating formula, and rather than disputation_oracle or judgment_oracle because the verses are narrative notice, not oracle speech. Under-3-verse row, disclosed as a two-verse unit bounded by 33:21's dateline — itself a tier-1 onset, one of the 14 in the book — and the pe after 33:22.

P09-009.device_notes: 39.17 carries two paseq occurrences on the one verse (count-only, single-witness); no K/Q or editorial note falls in this span. The onset is a sub-onset: it shares 38.1's governing word-event frame, but it turns the address from Gog to the birds and beasts, and that addressee change licenses it. Held at medium because the seam behind it carries a mark and no formula — one samekh stands after MT 39:16 in this witness, single witness.

P09-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: the far face carries a samekh and no close-role formula — that verse ends וָאַסְתִּ֥ר פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.39.24; WLC/OSHB, single witness) — and on the near face a messenger formula reopens at oshb:Ezek.39.25 לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה עַתָּ֗ה אָשִׁיב֙ אֶת שבית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְרִֽחַמְתִּ֖י כָּל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְקִנֵּאתִ֖י לְשֵׁ֥ם קָדְשִֽׁי on the word ‘therefore,’ immediately turning from the exile retrospective to the restoration promise — the addressee does not change across that turn, so it is a discourse turn and not a licensed sub-onset; the ketiv here reads שבית (oshb:Ezek.39.25, ketiv) and the qere reads שְׁב֣וּת (oshb:Ezek.39.25, Qere) (a single-witness textual-variant site, disclosed, never argued as a boundary). Close: 39.25-29 ends at oshb:Ezek.39.29 וְלֹֽא אַסְתִּ֥יר ע֛וֹד פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁפַ֤כְתִּי אֶת רוּחִי֙ עַל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה, the standard utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature (one of 81 book-wide) with a pe mark recorded immediately after -- the close evidence the restoration collection's own boundary is anchored on, matching the point where the following material opens on a dateline plus hand-of-YHWH and transport at Ezek.40.1. The close is therefore two-faced and top grade on both faces, while the onset stands on a mark behind and a discourse turn ahead: that is the shape this row's medium records.

P07-008.boundary_rationale: Onset side: the hard-seam dateline at oshb:Ezek.32.17 (year 12, day 15, with no month word in the verse, against the twelfth month named at 32:1; perfect hayah word-event form) opens onto the son-of-man command at oshb:Ezek.32.18 to “wail for the multitude of Egypt” (web:Ezek.32.18) -- a different technical verb from the qinah noun that opened and closed 32:1-16, disclosed as a genre question rather than assumed continuous with it. Close side: the row runs through the taunt (32:19-21) and the protected, never-cut roster of fallen nations in Sheol (32:22-30) to the doubled utterance-formula close at oshb:Ezek.32.31 and oshb:Ezek.32.32, corroborated by a following pe, at the book's own P6 parent-collection close. The genre question is held, not resolved, and does not bear on the seam grade. Both seams stand two-faced and top grade: 32:16 ends on the utterance signature, verse-final, with a pe after it, and 32:32 likewise ends verse-final on that signature with a pe, against a fresh strict word-event opening past this close. Inside the row the utterance at 32:31 is paragraph-final, since 32:32 opens on כִּֽי (oshb:Ezek.32.32; WLC/OSHB, single witness) with no onset-class device after it, and 32:18's son-of-man address corroborates the onset rather than opening a unit of its own; no rival of a licensed class stands at either seam, and the row's sixteen-verse length is the extent of the Sheol roster itself.
P07-008.device_notes: The roster at oshb:Ezek.32.22-Ezek.32.30 is a numbered/refrain list, each nation introduced by its own recurring formula, and no internal formula recurrence cuts inside it. Genre held between oracle_against_nation (the default) and lament_qinah with disclosure: the unit is introduced by a wail-verb (oshb:Ezek.32.18) rather than the qinah noun the unit at 32:1-16 uses at its own onset and colophon, so this row is typed oracle_against_nation with the relationship to the preceding qinah disclosed rather than assumed. paseq at oshb:Ezek.32.24 (count-only, single-witness). K/Q at oshb:Ezek.32.31 and oshb:Ezek.32.32. oshb:Ezek.32.30 carries an OSHB accent-divergence note and oshb:Ezek.32.32 a ketiv/qere-divergence note, both single-witness. The row closes at 32:32 with a doubled utterance formula (32:31 and 32:32) and a single-witness pe, matching the book's own P6 parent-collection close. MT 32:16 ends on the utterance signature, verse-final, and carries a following pe, single witness, at this unit's own onset seam. onset bytes (oshb:Ezek.32.17): וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר | close bytes (oshb:Ezek.32.32): כִּֽי נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת חתיתו בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חַיִּ֑ים וְהֻשְׁכַּב֩ בְּת֨וֹךְ עֲרֵלִ֜ים אֶת חַלְלֵי חֶ֗רֶב פַּרְעֹה֙ וְכָל הֲמוֹנֹ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה

P08-012.boundary_rationale: Onset: a samekh follows MT 36:15 (single-witness), the paragraph mark behind this unit's onset. A fresh strict-form word-event formula crosses a hard seam at Ezek.36.16 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.36.16), the fifth such hard seam since Ezek.33.1 (33.1, 33.23, 34.1, 35.1, 36.16) and not the last — 37.15 and 38.1 follow. 'Son of man' at Ezek.36.17 בֶּן אָדָ֗ם בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשְׁבִ֣ים עַל אַדְמָתָ֔ם וַיְטַמְּא֣וּ אוֹתָ֔הּ בְּדַרְכָּ֖ם וּבַעֲלִֽילוֹתָ֑ם כְּטֻמְאַת֙ הַנִּדָּ֔ה הָיְתָ֥ה דַרְכָּ֖ם לְפָנָֽי (oshb:Ezek.36.17) opens a retrospective on Israel's own defilement of the land and the resulting exile — a distinct tense and topic from the 'mountains of Israel' address just closed. Inside the span a samekh follows MT 36:21 (single-witness); the unit does not cut there because the messenger-formula pivot at Ezek.36.22 לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר לְבֵֽית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לֹ֧א לְמַעַנְכֶ֛ם אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י אִם לְשֵׁם קָדְשִׁי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חִלַּלְתֶּ֔ם בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אתֶם שָֽׁם (oshb:Ezek.36.22) (“I don't do this for your sake” (web:Ezek.36.22)) opens with a 'therefore' consequence-clause: it draws out the result of the profanation narrated in the third person at Ezek.36.20 וַיָּב֗וֹא אֶל הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֣אוּ שָׁ֔ם וַֽיְחַלְּל֖וּ אֶת שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י בֶּאֱמֹ֤ר לָהֶם֙ עַם יְהוָ֣ה אֵ֔לֶּה וּמֵאַרְצ֖וֹ יָצָֽאוּ (oshb:Ezek.36.20) and Ezek.36.21 וָאֶחְמֹ֖ל עַל שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י אֲשֶׁ֤ר חִלְּל֨וּהוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁמָּה (oshb:Ezek.36.21), where 'my holy name' is twice named as the thing profaned, and the same holy-name argument runs from there through 36.22 to the utterance close at 36.23. The turn from third-person narration to second-person address at 36.22 is disclosed here as a sub-onset within that one argument, not as an addressee change that would cut the unit. Close: the utterance formula at Ezek.36.23 וְקִדַּשְׁתִּ֞י אֶת שְׁמִ֣י הַגָּד֗וֹל הַֽמְחֻלָּל֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר חִלַּלְתֶּ֖ם בְּתוֹכָ֑ם וְיָדְע֨וּ הַגּוֹיִ֜ם כִּי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה בְּהִקָּדְשִׁ֥י בָכֶ֖ם לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.36.23), whose own bytes carry, immediately before the utterance formula, a recognition clause addressed to the nations, one of the 64 such verses book-wide and refrain-grade in class. Both that clause and the utterance signature stand mid-verse: the verse runs on after נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה with a dependent temporal infinitive, and no mark is recorded on it. Its far face, 36.24, opens on no particle of any tracked class, belongs to no device class and carries no mark (oshb:Ezek.36.24); a close whose near face is refrain-grade in class but mid-verse in position, against an empty far face, is the shape this row's medium records.
P08-012.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through the gather/cleanse/new-heart material of 36.24-32 as one continuous salvation_oracle. Rejected because 36.23's recognition-plus-utterance material runs from the major disjunctive through to the verse's last word, its formula tokens standing mid-verse with only a dependent temporal infinitive (בְּהִקָּדְשִׁ֥י בָכֶ֖ם לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם, oshb:Ezek.36.23; WLC/OSHB, single witness) after them, which grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal and not the weak mid-verse shape, and 36.24 opens the actual return and renewal rather than continuing 36.16-23's retrospective argument about the profaned name — no particle stands there in the Hebrew, and the English version's ‘For’ is translation wording that argues no boundary; splitting here keeps both resulting rows inside the 7-10 typical band.

P04-008.boundary_rationale: Every reference in this row touches MT ch 21 and is written dual. Onset: a strict word-event formula at web:Ezek.21.8 = oshb:Ezek.21.13 (וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר), a hard seam. Close: the emphatic I-YHWH-have-spoken formula at web:Ezek.21.17 = oshb:Ezek.21.22 (וְגַם אֲנִ֗י אַכֶּ֤ה כַפִּי֙ אֶל כַּפִּ֔י וַהֲנִחֹתִ֖י חֲמָתִ֑י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי), with a pe immediately after. Both outer seams are two-faced and top grade: a pe stands in this witness immediately before the word-event onset verse (single witness), and the close formula carries a pe after it with a fresh word-event opening past that. The poem's own refrains, sharpened and polished, the sword doubled and then tripled, run between the two; the one interior seam that carries real evidence on both faces is weighed below and held as a paragraph, and that held rival is the granularity judgement this row's medium carries.

P03-014.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:1 opens on the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.18.1); 18:2 quotes the popular proverb the oracle will refute, אָבוֹת֙ יֹ֣אכְלוּ בֹ֔סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י הַבָּנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה (oshb:Ezek.18.2) (“The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge”, web:Ezek.18.2). Close side: the span closes at 18:4, whose final clause הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֥יא תָמֽוּת (oshb:Ezek.18.4) ('the soul who sins shall die') states the disputation's thesis, and a samekh stands on this same verse in the single witness. An oath formula opens 18:3 ('as I live, declares the Lord YHWH') in its first five words, with the clause on the proverb's future use running on after it in the same verse, so it stands as texture inside the refutation and not as a row-final close. The onset seam is two-faced and top grade — the strict word-event at 18:1 against the I-YHWH-have-spoken formula, verse-final, with a pe after it behind the seam (oshb:Ezek.17.24) — while the close is a case turn inside one word-event unit, carrying no formula device on either face, with the samekh recorded there corroborating the close and not deciding it: that is the shape this row's medium_low records.

P03-015.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:5 opens with no formula device, the whole verse וְאִ֖ישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.5) ('if a man is righteous and does what is just and right'), a default case-law onset following the thesis stated at 18:4; the samekh recorded there, closing the unit before it, corroborates this row's onset from the far side of the seam. Close side: the row runs to 18:9, and its own final words are the utterance formula חָיֹ֣ה יִֽחְיֶ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.9), a genuine verse-final refrain closing the first case before the wicked son's case opens at 18:10 with no formula of its own. Both of this row's seams are case turns inside one word-event unit: at the onset the samekh recorded on 18:4 behind the seam corroborates and does not decide, with no formula device on either face, and at the close the verse-final utterance at 18:9 stands paragraph-final, since 18:10 brings no fresh onset and no mark falls at that seam. That is the shape this row's medium_low records.
P03-015.strongest_rejected_alternative: No parashah mark corroborates a seam at 18:9; keeping 18:5-9 fused with 18:10-20 into one eleven-plus-five-verse row was weighed and not taken because the utterance formula there is genuinely verse-final, unlike its mid-verse recurrences elsewhere in MT 18 (18:3, 18:23, 18:30, 18:32).

P03-016.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:10 opens with no formula device, the whole verse וְהוֹלִ֥יד בֵּן פָּרִ֖יץ שֹׁפֵ֣ךְ דָּ֑ם וְעָ֣שָׂה אָ֔ח מֵאַחַ֖ד מֵאֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Ezek.18.10) ('and he fathers a violent son who sheds blood'), continuing the case-law series by default. The righteous grandson's case (18:14) and the summary restatement (18:19-20) follow without any fresh formula onset of their own, since 18:18 explicitly recalls the father's own guilt from 18:10-13 before drawing the general rule -- one continuous legal argument across three generations, not three independently onset units. Close side: the row runs through 18:20; its opening clause הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֣יא תָמ֑וּת בֵּ֞ן לֹא יִשָּׂ֣א בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֗ב (oshb:Ezek.18.20) ('the soul who sins shall die; a son shall not bear his father's iniquity') restates 18:4's thesis and closes the argument, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse. Behind the onset the preceding verse ends on the utterance formula, which stands paragraph-final there because 18:10 brings no fresh onset, and no mark falls at that seam; ahead of 18:20's samekh the next case turn opens with no formula of its own. Both seams are case turns inside one word-event unit, the close corroborated by a samekh that does not decide it and the onset carrying no mark at all: that is the shape this row's medium_low records.

P03-017.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:21 opens with no formula device, וְהָרָשָׁ֗ע כִּ֤י יָשׁוּב֙ (oshb:Ezek.18.21) (“But if the wicked turns from all his sins that he has committed”, web:Ezek.18.21), a default onset for the repentance case; the running text reads the ketiv חטאתו (oshb:Ezek.18.21) in place of the pointed form. Close side: the row ends at 18:23, the whole verse הֶחָפֹ֤ץ אֶחְפֹּץ֙ מ֣וֹת רָשָׁ֔ע נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הֲל֛וֹא בְּשׁוּב֥וֹ מִדְּרָכָ֖יו וְחָיָֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.23), matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse. The oath-adjacent utterance formula sits mid-verse there ('declares the Lord YHWH'), with the verse’s own final clause, “and not rather that he should return from his way, and live?” (web:Ezek.18.23), still to follow; the samekh recorded on the verse corroborates that close and does not decide it. The seam itself is a case turn inside one word-event unit: the utterance formula inside 18:23 is mid-verse and so carries no close role, and the case past the seam opens with no formula device of its own; the onset seam behind, marked by the samekh after 18:20, is the same shape, a case turn with no formula on either face. That is what this row's medium_low records.

P03-018.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:24 opens with no formula device, וּבְשׁ֨וּב צַדִּ֤יק מִצִּדְקָתוֹ֙ וְעָ֣שָׂה עָ֔וֶל (oshb:Ezek.18.24) (“But when the righteous turns away from his righteousness, and commits iniquity”, web:Ezek.18.24), the reverse case answering 18:21-23; the running text reads the ketiv צדקתו in place of the pointed form. Close side: 18:26 closes the row; its final clause בְּעַוְל֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֖ה יָמֽוּת (oshb:Ezek.18.26) ('for the injustice he has done he dies') restates the case's rule, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse. Israel's objection is quoted between the case and its restatement, at 18:25, inside this same span. Both seams are case turns inside one word-event unit, each corroborated by a samekh that does not decide it — the one recorded after 18:23 behind the onset, the one on 18:26 at the close — and neither carries a seam-role formula on either face, 18:23's own utterance formula standing mid-verse there: that is the shape this row's medium_low records.

P03-019.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:27 opens with no formula device, וּבְשׁ֣וּב רָשָׁ֗ע מֵֽרִשְׁעָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.18.27) ('again, when a wicked person turns from the wickedness he has committed'), the positive repentance case answering 18:24-26; the running text reads the ketiv וישוב (oshb:Ezek.18.28) at 18:28. Israel's objection recurs at 18:29, where a single-witness OSHB editorial note stands. The judgment proper then opens at 18:30 with לָכֵן֩ אִ֨ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֜יו אֶשְׁפֹּ֤ט אֶתְכֶם֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.18.30) (“Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, everyone according to his ways”, web:Ezek.18.30); the formula embedded there is the utterance formula, and no messenger formula falls in this span. Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own end, 18:32, whose final clause וְהָשִׁ֖יבוּ וִֽחְיֽוּ (oshb:Ezek.18.32) ('so turn, and live') closes the chapter, matched by a pe recorded on this same verse; the utterance formula recurs mid-verse there rather than at the very end, so it is the plain imperative clause and the pe mark, not the formula's position, that anchor this close. The onset seam is a case turn inside one word-event unit, carrying no formula device on either face, with the samekh after 18:26 behind it corroborating and not deciding: that is the shape this row's medium_low records.

P09-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: the verse opens on the hand-of-YHWH idiom immediately followed by a transport verb, oshb:Ezek.37.1 הָיְתָ֣ה עָלַי֮ יַד יְהוָה֒ וַיּוֹצִאֵ֤נִי בְר֨וּחַ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיְנִיחֵ֖נִי בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבִּקְעָ֑ה וְהִ֖יא מְלֵאָ֥ה עֲצָמֽוֹת -- the same onset shape that opens the book's other three long prose visions, and this occurrence is one of only 7 hand-of-YHWH verses in the book. The unit is held as one scene, with the live rival inside it weighed below: the prophet is set down among the bones (37.1-2), questioned and commanded to prophesy twice -- once to the bones, once to the breath/spirit (37.4-6, 37.9), watches the two-stage reanimation (37.7-8, 37.10), and receives the scene's own interpretation as a word to 'son of man' (oshb:Ezek.37.11 וַיֹּאמֶר֮ אֵלַי֒ בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑מָּה הִנֵּ֣ה אֹמְרִ֗ים יָבְשׁ֧וּ עַצְמוֹתֵ֛ינוּ וְאָבְדָ֥ה תִקְוָתֵ֖נוּ נִגְזַ֥רְנוּ לָֽנוּ). Close: oshb:Ezek.37.14 stacks three refrain-grade closes in one verse -- the second-person plural recognition variant ('and you will know that I am YHWH', part of a 21-verse 2mp family sweep), the emphatic 'I YHWH have spoken' close (one of 14 book-wide), and the short utterance signature without the divine-name pair (one of only 4 such short forms in the book) -- וְנָתַתִּ֨י רוּחִ֤י בָכֶם֙ וִחְיִיתֶ֔ם וְהִנַּחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם עַל אַדְמַתְכֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֞ם כִּי אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִׂ֖יתִי נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, and a pe mark is recorded immediately after this verse (tier-3 single-witness, informing not deciding). Both sides of the following seam were weighed: oshb:Ezek.37.15 opens with the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, one of 39 verses carrying that strict form, so the close at 37.14 and the fresh onset at 37.15 corroborate each other from both directions. Both faces of that close are top grade; the row is held at medium because a licensed rival stands inside the span, at the 37.10/37.11 seam.
P09-001.strongest_rejected_alternative: A split inside the scene at the 37.10/37.11 seam, which is live and licensed rather than mark-only: a samekh stands on oshb:Ezek.37.10 behind it (tier-3 single-witness), and ahead of it oshb:Ezek.37.11 opens 'he said to me' with the son-of-man address, a default onset inside a vision, while oshb:Ezek.37.12 carries a messenger formula and a second samekh continuing the same rival. Read that way 37.1-10 would be a complete scene — command, prophecy, result — and 37.11-14 its interpretation with its own recognition close. The span is nevertheless kept whole as one vision_report unit, the question of which recognition clause closes it held rather than decided here; the other 'he said to me' verses (37.3, 37.4, 37.9) are dialogue turns that yield no scene-complete piece and are not live rivals, and 37.2's transport verb would leave a one-verse remainder.
P09-001.device_notes: 37.2 and 37.9 each carry one paseq (count-only, single-witness, no intra-verse position sourceable from the extract). 37.9 also carries an OSHB editorial note recording an accent divergence from BHS (single-witness apparatus, not a text variant). The WEB prints a mid-verse paragraph inside 37.3 (“Son of man, can these bones live?” (web:Ezek.37.3), then the prophet's reply) -- tier-4 texture, cited only and never a boundary argument. The witness also records a samekh after MT 36:38 (single witness), the paragraph mark behind this row's onset. The second-person plural recognition variant stands inside the scene at 37.6 as well as at the close, disclosed here and arguing no boundary.

P09-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: no word-event, messenger, hand-of-YHWH or address formula opens 39.21; the seam rests on the verse-final utterance formula standing at 39.20 behind it — no mark is recorded on that verse, and the formula stands there alone — and on the topical turn from the birds-and-beasts summons to a first-person retrospective on Israel's exile. This retrospective carries the wide-family recognition close addressed to “the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.39.22) at 39.22 (one of the expansions in the 64-verse wide sweep, not the strict 28), internal and paragraph-final rather than row-final. The knowing-clause at 39.23 is addressed to the nations but carries no divine-name predicate and belongs to no tracked family; that family's nations-addressed member in this chapter stands outside this span. Close: 39.21-24 ends at oshb:Ezek.39.24 כְּטֻמְאָתָ֥ם וּכְפִשְׁעֵיהֶ֖ם עָשִׂ֣יתִי אֹתָ֑ם וָאַסְתִּ֥ר פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶֽם, with a samekh mark recorded immediately after (tier-3 single-witness); 39.25 then reopens with a fresh messenger formula, weighed from the far side of the seam. The onset's own near face carries no device of any tracked class, which is what this row's low records.

P02-008.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.1 וַתִּשָּׂ֨א אֹתִ֜י ר֗וּחַ וַתָּבֵ֣א אֹ֠תִי אֶל שַׁ֨עַר בֵּית יְהוָ֤ה הַקַּדְמוֹנִי֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ימָה וְהִנֵּה֙ בְּפֶ֣תַח הַשַּׁ֔עַר עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ וָאֶרְאֶ֨ה בְתוֹכָ֜ם אֶת יַאֲזַנְיָ֧ה בֶן עַזֻּ֛ר וְאֶת פְּלַטְיָ֥הוּ בֶן בְּנָיָ֖הוּ שָׂרֵ֖י הָעָֽם — a fresh transport (“the Spirit lifted me up and brought me” (web:Ezek.11.1)) to the east gate, introducing new participants (Jaazaniah son of Azzur, Pelatiah son of Benaiah). A pe follows this very verse (single-witness), falling inside the row between its first verse and the next — a mid-row mark disclosed and not cut, as the mark at 11:6 is. The onset rests instead on the transport itself, the two verbs that open it, a predicate-class member with two tokens and one of exactly two such transports in the book; behind it the far face carries no mark and no formula, and chapter 10 carries no parashah mark at all. Close: oshb:Ezek.11.13 וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּהִנָּ֣בְאִ֔י וּפְלַטְיָ֥הוּ בֶן בְּנָיָ֖ה מֵ֑ת וָאֶפֹּ֨ל עַל פָּנַ֜י וָאֶזְעַ֣ק קוֹל גָּד֗וֹל וָאֹמַר֙ אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה כָּלָה֙ אַתָּ֣ה עֹשֶׂ֔ה אֵ֖ת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל — Pelatiah's death and the prophet's cry “Ah Lord Yahweh! Will you make a full end of the remnant of Israel?” (web:Ezek.11.13) — is a narrative close; a pe follows this verse as well (single-witness), the close-side mark this row reads. Both near faces carry licensed evidence — the transport at the onset, the narrative close and its pe at the end — while the onset's far face is bare: that is the shape this row's medium records. Both sides: the courtyard scene runs as one continuous unit from the transport to the prophet's cry, with a sub-onset at oshb:Ezek.11.5 “Yahweh's Spirit fell on me, and he said to me, 'Speak …” (web:Ezek.11.5) that introduces direct judgment speech but carries no word-event formula and is not itself an addressee-class shift, so it is disclosed as internal texture rather than a competing row seam.
